The Dutch government is recruiting Supervising veterinarians for slaughterhouses across the Netherlands. Your work protects animal welfare, animal health, and food safety. This is a meaningful role with real impact on society. In September 2026, the Dutch government will start the next training program for Supervising veterinarians.About the roleAs a Supervising Veterinarian, you supervise the entire slaughter process in your region. From the arrival of live animals to the final inspection, you ensure that all steps meet legal and professional standards. You act when rules are not followed and help maintain public trust in safe, responsible food production.What you’ll do• Conduct ante- and post-mortem inspections• Identify diseases and abnormalities that may pose risks• Monitor hygiene practices and compliance with legislation• Safeguard animal welfare throughout the process• Work independently in the slaughterhouse while supported by a team of veterinarians and inspectors• Contribute to continuous improvement with colleagues and policymakers• Communicate clearly, including in stressful situationsTraining and relocation supportInternational candidates receive full guidance when moving to the Netherlands. You get:• A fully paid 16-month training program• An intensive Dutch language course up to B2 level• Professional development and career progression opportunities• Support with relocation, housing, and administrative arrangementsEmployment conditionsYou work under Dutch public sector employment conditions:• Salary: scale 10 during training (€3,404–€5,389) and scale 11 after certification (€4,024–€6,110), 36 hours• You will start with a temporary contract for the duration of the training program, from 21 September 2026 to 1 February 2028.o    With positive progress and a satisfactory evaluation, this will be followed by a one-year temporary contract.o    After a successful evaluation at the end of that period, you will be offered a permanent contract.• 24–36 hour workweek• Individual Choice Budget (16.5 percent of annual salary)• 144 vacation hours + 64 IKB hours (full-time)• Pension with ABP• Mobility card or bicycle allowance• Company lease car for work, with private-use option• Paid travel time and flexible working arrangements• Training and coaching opportunitiesWho we’re looking forYou work accurately and responsibly, even under pressure. You stay calm in complex situations and make well-founded decisions. You collaborate easily across disciplines and value the responsibility of protecting public health, food safety, and animal welfare.Job requirements• You hold a veterinary degree that qualifies for Dutch Veterinary Register registration.• You speak English at B2 level and are willing to learn Dutch.• You hold a category B driving licence.• You are prepared to relocate and complete the full training program.• Experience in the veterinary or food sector is an advantage.• You work independently and carefully in a regulated environment.Competencies• analyzing• judgement• collaboration• planning and organizing• perseverance• stress resilienceSelection process• Pre-selection based on CV and motivation letter• Mandatory online information session: 29 January or 26 February• Intake interview: 2 February till 1 April• Written case study and first formal interview: 11 February till 13 April• English language test and competency assessment: 24 February till 29 may• Second interview: 8 April till 12 June• Employment conditions discussion: June*Please note: the dates are provisional and may still be subject to change

Imagine this: you’re behind the wheel of a modern bus, smoothly navigating through the streets of Utrecht, Arnhem or Nijmegen.  No turn too sharp, no intersection too busy. Along the way, you share a friendly word with your passengers while keeping a watchful eye on their safety and comfort.As a bus driver at Transdev – the largest mobility company in the Netherlands – you contribute daily to freedom and mobility. A new country. A modern dental practice. And the opportunity to become an important part of a team that is building for the future.At Steenwijkerdiep, you will work as a General Dentist in a professional and well-equipped group practice in Steenwijk. You will be surrounded by experienced colleagues, have access to modern equipment and high-quality materials, and receive support with the practical steps involved in starting your career in the Netherlands.Your roleAs a General Dentist at Steenwijkerdiep, you will provide a broad range of general dental care to your patients.You will work in a professional environment where patient-centred care, quality and teamwork are central. You will have the freedom and resources to focus on good dentistry, while being supported by an experienced team around you.This position also offers the opportunity to become an important part of the future of the practice. There is room for you to take on a key role within the team and grow with the practice over time.About SteenwijkerdiepSteenwijkerdiep is a modern dental practice located in Steenwijk, the Netherlands.Our group practice offers a broad scope of dental care and consists of a multidisciplinary team of dentists, dental hygienists and dental assistants. By combining professional expertise with advanced equipment and high-quality materials, we aim to provide our patients with the highest possible standard of care.The atmosphere within the practice is professional, collaborative and patient-focused.What we are looking forFor this position, you have:•    Completed a relevant study in the sector Health-technical professions at WO/Master’s degree level;•    A minimum B1 level of English and the willingness to learn the Dutch language;•    A minimum of 3 months’ work experience as a dentist;•    A category B driving licence.What we offerYou can expect:•    A salary between €3,300 and €5,500 gross per month, depending on qualifications and experience;•    An annual contract for 32–40 hours per week, with the intention of offering a permanent contract;•    Variable working hours;•    Excellent secondary employment conditions;•    A modern and professional workplace;•    Support with finding accommodation;•    Support and information regarding the recognition of your foreign diploma and your possibilities to work during that period.A practical start in the NetherlandsMoving abroad for work involves more than simply finding the right job. Having a place to live from the start makes that transition considerably easier. Accommodation is available at two residential parks, both located approximately 4–5 kilometres by bicycle from the practice. The homes can be rented for a minimum period of three months, subject to availability, with several accommodation options available for different situations.This gives you the possibility to arrange accommodation close to your workplace when you first arrive in the Netherlands, giving you time to settle into your new job and surroundings without having to immediately search for housing on your own.Interested in joining Steenwijkerdiep?We are looking for a General Dentist who values high-quality care, enjoys working as part of a professional team and would like to build a long-term career in the Netherlands.For more information about the position, the recognition process for your foreign diploma, the possibilities to work during this period or the application process, please contact: iris.vermeer@uwv.nl
